subject: CAF-2 Taxation: Principles and Compliance
finance_act_note: The Examinable Editions notice names only the Sep-26 study-text edition; no Finance Act is named. Treat 'Finance Act 2026 amendments incorporated' as INFERENCE, not fact.

areas.title: Objective, System, Constitutional Provisions and Ethics

topics.title: Basic Concepts of Taxation and Constitutional Provisions

los.paraphrase: Talk through what direct versus indirect taxation means in practice and why the distinction matters.
Outline what the Federal Consolidated Fund and the Public Account are.
Outline what the Provincial Consolidated Fund and the Public Account are.
Explain which taxes Parliament is empowered to impose.
Explain the tax-raising powers available to provincial assemblies.
Discuss why the state may levy taxes and the limits on that right, leaving out the classic canons of taxation.
Discuss the moral case for taxpayers and tax practitioners complying with tax law.
Contrast the legal powers of tax authorities with their ethical responsibilities.
Explain the four pillars of tax administration: fairness, transparency, equity and accountability.
Draw the basic line between tax evasion and tax avoidance.
Describe the core concepts of income and how far the income-tax charge reaches.

topics.title: Chargeability and Computation of Income and Tax

los.paraphrase: Work out income, taxable income and the tax on it under each head — salary, property, business, capital gains and other sources — for non-corporate taxpayers.
Apply the rules on loss carry-forward, deductible allowances, set-off of losses, tax credits and exemptions/concessions.

areas.title: Income Tax Laws – Administration and Compliance

los.paraphrase: Explain the main tax-compliance duties and the filings they require.
Identify who has to file an income-tax return and a wealth statement.
Explain how returns/statements are filed and revised, the due dates, and how extensions work.
Draft a return of income and a wealth statement, including the reconciliation between them.
Explain the different types of assessment under the law.
Cover the audit of a person's income-tax affairs and how long records must be kept.
Describe the appeal route: Commissioner (Appeals), Appellate Tribunal and the High Court.
State the law on alternative dispute resolution.
Compute output and input sales tax on taxable supplies, including zero-rated and exempt supplies.
Explain when sales-tax liability arises and how it is paid.
Apportion input tax and work out carry-forward and refunds.
Describe the types of registration, the requirements, and the procedures for registering, de-registering and filing returns.
List the records a registered person must maintain, the retention rules, and the audit procedures around them.
Explain why tax invoices, debit notes and credit notes matter and what the rules require of them.
Explain the procedure for destruction of goods.
